mainTopic: How מעשר שני and בכורים compare to תרומה: the rules for an אונן and ביעור, and the sources for the laws of burning and eating them when impure.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier proof. The list of differences between מעשר שני/בכורים and תרומה is not complete, so the תנא 'taught and left things out' (תני ושייר). The גמרא then explains two disputes. The רבנן compare בכורים to מעשר through a הקש, so בכורים are forbidden to an אונן and need ביעור. רבי שמעון notes that the תורה calls בכורים 'תרומה,' so he permits them to an אונן and exempts them from ביעור. Next the גמרא finds the sources for the rules about impure מעשר. 'לא בערתי ממנו בטמא' forbids burning it, and 'לא תוכל לאכול בשעריך' gives a לאו against eating it when the food itself is impure. The word 'ממנו' lets impure תרומה oil be burned but not impure קודש, because קודש is stricter: it has more stringencies, or it carries כרת. Eating impure תרומה is still forbidden but brings no lashes, because it is a לאו הבא מכלל עשה. At the end, רב אשי starts another proof of תני ושייר, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The list leaves things out, so the תנא taught and omitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to another difference between מעשר שני/בכורים and תרומה that the משנה does not mention. This proves the תנא sometimes leaves cases out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another difference is that someone who eats them while they themselves are impure gets lashes, which is not so with תרומה. The משנה does not teach this. So clearly, the תנא taught some differences and left others out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an earlier proof. It shows that the משנה's list of differences is not complete, so the תנא clearly 'taught and left things out.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating impure מעשר שני or בכורים earns lashes, but the same is not true for impure תרומה. The משנה still does not list this difference. Since the list is clearly incomplete, the fact that a case is missing (like the ערל eating מעשר שני) proves nothing about the halacha.

keyTerms.meaning: their own impurity, meaning the food itself is impure (not the person)
he receives lashes
the portion of produce given to a כהן
apparently, so clearly
he taught and left out; the list is not complete

steps.whatToRemember: A missing case in a list does not prove anything, because this תנא is known to leave items out (תני ושייר).
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'טומאת עצמן' as 'the person is impure.' It means the food is impure, even if the person eating it is pure.

phrases.english: and one who eats them when they themselves are impure is lashed,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means מעשר שני and בכורים, the two foods the משנה was comparing to תרומה.

phrases.english: which is not so with תרומה —
this it does not teach.
Apparently, he taught and left things out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier argument from the previous part of the daf about whether a missing case proves anything.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's list is incomplete (תני ושייר), so leaving out a case is not evidence of a lenient ruling.

steps.title: Quoting the אונן dispute and asking for its source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: these foods are forbidden to an אונן, but רבי שמעון permits. It then asks where the רבנן learn this.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they are forbidden to an אונן, and רבי שמעון permits.' From where do the רבנן learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to explaining the משנה line by line. It quotes the אונן rule and asks for the source of the רבנן's view, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says both מעשר שני and בכורים are forbidden to an אונן. רבי שמעון disagrees about בכורים. The question 'מנא להו' asks for the פסוק behind the רבנן's strict view on בכורים.

keyTerms.meaning: a mourner in the first stage of mourning, right after a close relative's death
permits
first fruits brought to the מקדש
from where do they know this?

phrases.english: And they are forbidden to an acute mourner,
and Rabbi Shimon permits.
phrases.notes: He permits בכורים to an אונן; everyone agrees מעשר שני is forbidden.

phrases.english: From where do they derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the proof about תני ושייר to explaining the content of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the רבנן's ruling that בכורים are forbidden to an אונן.

steps.title: The רבנן learn it from a הקש to מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק lists 'תרומת ידך' (בכורים) together with מעשר. Since מעשר is forbidden to an אונן, בכורים are too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'You may not eat in your gates the tithe of your grain, your wine and your oil, and the offering of your hand.' The Master said that 'the offering of your hand' means בכורים. So בכורים are put side by side with מעשר. Just as מעשר is forbidden to an אונן, so are בכורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. בכורים appear in the same list as מעשר, so they share its rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'תרומת ידך' are explained as בכורים. Because the פסוק places them next to מעשר, a הקש (comparison by placement) applies. מעשר is already known to be forbidden to an אונן, so בכורים get the same rule.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is written
'the offering of your hand,' explained as בכורים
they are compared by placement in the פסוק (a הקש)

steps.whyThisMatters: This הקש is the backbone of the רבנן's whole approach. They will use it again for ביעור.

phrases.english: As it is written: "You may not eat within your gates
the tithe of your grain, your wine, and your oil, etc.,
and the offering of your hand,"
and the Master said:
"The offering of your hand" — these are the first fruits,
and first fruits are compared to tithe:
just as tithe is forbidden to an acute mourner,
so too first fruits are forbidden to an acute mourner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A הקש in דברים 12:17 places בכורים ('תרומת ידך') next to מעשר, so like מעשר they are forbidden to an אונן.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: בכורים are called תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון argues that since the תורה calls בכורים 'תרומה,' they follow תרומה's rule, and תרומה is permitted to an אונן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: the תורה called them 'תרומה.' Just as תרומה is permitted to an אונן, so are בכורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי שמעון's side. He reads the same פסוק differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use the same words 'תרומת ידך.' The רבנן focus on where בכורים are placed (next to מעשר). רבי שמעון focuses on what they are called (תרומה), and since תרומה is permitted to an אונן, so are בכורים.

keyTerms.meaning: the Merciful One (the תורה) called them
permitted

steps.whatToRemember: Same פסוק, two readings: the רבנן follow the placement (next to מעשר), while רבי שמעון follows the name (תרומה).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon: the Merciful One called them teruma,
phrases.notes: He's pointing to the word 'תרומת' in the same פסוק.

phrases.english: just as teruma is permitted to an acute mourner,
so too first fruits are permitted to an acute mourner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי שמעון's opposing reading of the same פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בכורים are named 'תרומה,' so like תרומה they are permitted to an אונן.

steps.title: Quoting the dispute about ביעור
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says these foods must be removed at the time of ביעור, but רבי שמעון exempts בכורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they require removal, and רבי שמעון exempts.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. This sets up the explanation of the dispute in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ביעור is the duty to clear out tithes and holy produce from the house at a set time. The רבנן include בכורים in this duty, while רבי שמעון exempts them.

keyTerms.meaning: removal of tithes and holy produce from one's possession at a set time
they are obligated
exempts

phrases.english: And they require eradication,
and Rabbi Shimon exempts.
phrases.notes: He exempts בכורים; מעשר שני still needs ביעור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next ruling in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעשר שני and בכורים require ביעור; רבי שמעון exempts בכורים.

steps.title: The ביעור dispute depends on the הקש
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן apply the הקש of בכורים to מעשר here too, so בכורים need ביעור. רבי שמעון does not apply it.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage compares them, and one Sage does not compare them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the ביעור dispute in one short line. It all depends on whether you use the הקש between בכורים and מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן compare בכורים to מעשר, so since מעשר needs ביעור, בכורים do too. רבי שמעון does not make this comparison, consistent with his reading in step 4, so בכורים are exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: one Sage (literally 'master')
applies the הקש comparison

steps.whatToRemember: Both disputes (אונן and ביעור) come from one root question: do we compare בכורים to מעשר (רבנן) or not (רבי שמעון)?

phrases.english: One Sage juxtaposes, and one Sage does not juxtapose.
phrases.notes: The first 'Sage' is the רבנן and the second is רבי שמעון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the dispute quoted in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The רבנן apply the הקש of בכורים to מעשר (so ביעור applies), while רבי שמעון does not (so בכורים are exempt).

steps.title: Where do we learn the rules about impure מעשר and בכורים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes two more rules from the משנה and asks for their source.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is forbidden to burn them when they are impure. Someone who eats them while they themselves are impure gets lashes. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes two more rules about מעשר שני and בכורים and asks where they come from. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two rules here. The first is that you may not burn these foods even when they are already impure. The second is that eating them when the food is impure brings מלקות, even if the person eating is pure.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means to burn or use up, for example as fuel
Impurity of the food itself, not of the person
Gets מלקות (lashes)
From where do we know this?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up this לבער with the ביעור from step 5. There, ביעור meant removing the produce at the set time. Here, לבער means burning it.

phrases.english: And it is forbidden to burn them when impure,
and one who eats them when they themselves are impure is flogged,
from where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next rules in the same משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the ban on burning impure מעשר and בכורים, and for the lashes for eating them when they are impure

steps.title: רבי שמעון reads the פסוק as covering both kinds of impurity
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'I did not use it while impure' covers both an impure person and impure food.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון says, 'I did not consume of it while impure' means both when I am impure and the food is pure, and when I am pure and the food is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי שמעון learns from one פסוק that מעשר may not be used in either kind of impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בטמא' does not say who is impure. So רבי שמעון reads it broadly: it covers an impure person and also impure food. 'בערתי' covers using it up in any way, including burning.

keyTerms.meaning: The declaration a person makes that he handled his מעשרות properly; this פסוק is part of it
I used up or consumed
While impure, without saying whether the person or the food is impure

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
"I did not consume of it while impure,"
whether I am impure and it is pure,
or whether I am pure and it is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The open-ended word 'בטמא' covers both an impure person and impure food, and 'בערתי' includes burning

steps.title: רבי שמעון does not know where the warning against eating is written
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that it does not know the actual warning (לאו) against eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: But where a person is warned against eating it, I do not know.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון admits that this פסוק shows it is forbidden, but he does not know where the actual warning is. This sets up the גמרא's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words of the declaration show that it is forbidden. But to give מלקות you need a real warning (אזהרה) in the תורה. רבי שמעון says he cannot find one.

keyTerms.meaning: Warned; has an actual prohibition (אזהרה) in the תורה
I do not know

phrases.english: But where one is warned against eating it,
I do not know.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵיכָא מוּזְהָר עַל אֲכִילָתוֹ אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא continues with a question about the source of the warning, which the גמרא challenges in step 10 and resolves in steps 11–12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating it is clearly forbidden, but the source of the formal warning is unknown

steps.title: But the warning for an impure person is written openly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges him: the תורה openly forbids an impure person to eat holy food.
steps.simpleTranslation: The warning for an impure person is written openly: 'A person who touches it will be impure until evening, and he may not eat from the holy foods unless he washes his body in water.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי שמעון could say he does not know the warning, when a פסוק openly forbids an impure person to eat holy food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For an impure person, the warning is right there in the פסוק. So the claim 'I do not know' seems wrong, at least for this kind of impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity of the person's body
Openly, in so many words
Holy foods; the גמרא later explains this includes מעשר שני

phrases.english: About bodily impurity it is written openly:

phrases.aramaic: ״נֶפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר תִּגַּע בּוֹ וְטָמְאָה עַד הָעָרֶב
phrases.english: "The soul that touches it shall be impure until the evening,
and he shall not eat from the holy things
unless he has washed his flesh in water"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim made in step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement 'I do not know where he is warned'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is an open warning against an impure person eating holy food, so the warning is known

steps.title: He was really asking about impure food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי שמעון's question was only about food that is itself impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he was asking: where do we learn the rule when the food itself is impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing רבי שמעון's question. He was only asking about food that is itself impure. Next it gives the source for that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The open פסוק covers only an impure person. When the food is impure and the person is pure, there is still no written warning. That is the gap רבי שמעון meant.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he was really asking
Impurity of the food itself

phrases.english: This is what he was asking:
From where do we learn about its own impurity?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון was asking about every kind of impurity
steps.terutzMaskana: He was only asking about food that is itself impure

steps.title: The source for impure מעשר: 'here you may not eat'
steps.stepSummary: Comparing two פסוקים 'בשעריך' shows that impure מעשר may not be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'You may not eat the tithe of your grain within your gates.' Elsewhere it says: 'Within your gates you shall eat it, the impure and the pure together, like the deer and the hart.' The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: even an impure person and a pure person may eat at one table, from one bowl, without worry. So the תורה is saying: what I allowed you there, 'eat it within your gates', here you may not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source. A פסוק about disqualified קדשים allows eating them 'בשעריך' in any state of impurity. A פסוק about מעשר says 'you may not eat בשעריך', so those same allowances are forbidden for מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'בשעריך' allowance for disqualified קדשים includes eating them even when the meat is impure. The 'לא תוכל' for מעשר takes that whole allowance away. So eating impure מעשר is covered by a לאו, which is why there are מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches
Within your gates, meaning in any city
Like a deer and a hart, which are animals with no holiness
A teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

steps.whatToRemember: There are two separate sources. Burning impure מעשר is forbidden because of 'לא בערתי ממנו בטמא'. Eating מעשר when the food is impure is under a לאו, learned from 'לא תוכל לאכול בשעריך'.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"You may not eat within your gates the tithe of your grain,"
and later it says
"Within your gates you shall eat it,
phrases.notes: דברים 15:22. This פסוק is about קדשים that became disqualified.

phrases.english: the impure and the pure together, like the gazelle and the hart,"
and the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ טָמֵא וְטָהוֹר אוֹכְלִין עַל שׁוּלְחָן אֶחָד
phrases.english: even an impure and a pure person may eat at one table
from one bowl, and they need not worry,
and the Merciful One says:
that which I told you there, "within your gates you shall eat it" —
here, do not eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the narrowed question of step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לא תוכל לאכול בשעריך' forbids for מעשר what 'בשעריך תאכלנו' allows for disqualified קדשים, including eating food that is itself impure
steps.whyThisMatters: This לאו is what makes it possible to give מלקות for eating מעשר when the food is impure.

steps.title: Why may impure תרומה be burned?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the burning ban does not apply to תרומה, and the גמרא asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not so with תרומה. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's contrast: the ban on burning does not apply to impure תרומה. It asks for the source, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impure מעשר may not be burned, but impure תרומה may. The גמרא wants to know what in the פסוקים creates this difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Which is not the case
The portion of produce given to the כהן

phrases.english: Which is not so with teruma.
From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the contrast with תרומה from the same משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that impure תרומה may be burned

steps.title: 'ממנו' means only מעשר, so impure תרומה oil may be burned
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן learns from the word 'ממנו' that only מעשר may not be burned when impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the פסוק says, 'I did not consume of it while impure.' Of it you may not burn, but you may burn oil of תרומה that became impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers that the word 'ממנו' ('of it') limits the burning ban to מעשר. So impure תרומה oil may be burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ממנו' points only to the food the פסוק is talking about, which is מעשר. This excludes everything else, so impure תרומה oil may be burned, for example as fuel.

keyTerms.meaning: Of it; this limits the rule to מעשר
Burns
תרומה oil that became impure

steps.whatToRemember: Impure מעשר may not be burned. Impure תרומה oil may be burned, because the word 'ממנו' limits the ban to מעשר.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
As the verse says:
"I did not consume of it while impure" —
of it you may not burn,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַתָּה מַבְעִיר שֶׁמֶן שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה שֶׁנִּטְמָא.
phrases.english: but you may burn oil of teruma that became impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'ממנו' limits the burning ban to מעשר, so impure תרומה oil may be burned

steps.title: Maybe 'of it' allows burning impure sacred oil
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that 'ממנו' might exclude impure קודש oil from the burning ban, rather than תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: 'of it' you may not burn, but you may burn sacred oil that became impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 14. Maybe the word 'ממנו' means only מעשר is banned, so impure קודש oil may be burned for light.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 used 'ממנו' (of it, meaning מעשר alone) to allow burning impure תרומה. The גמרא points out that the same word could just as easily allow burning impure קודש. Nothing so far shows which one is being excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: But say, maybe it means this instead
Burn, here meaning use as fuel for light
Oil that was dedicated to the בית המקדש
Became impure

phrases.english: But say: 'of it' you may not burn,
phrases.notes: 'Of it' means the מעשר that the פסוק is talking about.

phrases.english: but you may burn
sacred oil that became impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what רבי יוחנן's 'ממנו' excludes
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reading that 'ממנו' excludes תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word could exclude קודש just as well as תרומה

steps.title: A קל וחומר keeps sacred oil under the ban
steps.stepSummary: If light מעשר may not be burned while impure, then strict קודש surely may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it a קל וחומר? If for מעשר, which is lenient, the תורה said 'I did not burn of it while impure,' then for קודש, which is strict, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'ממנו' cannot exclude קודש. A קל וחומר shows קודש must be banned too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר is less holy than קודש. If the lighter thing is banned from being burned while impure, the stricter thing surely is. So 'ממנו' cannot be read as allowing impure קודש oil.

keyTerms.meaning: Logic from light to strict: if the lighter case has a rule, the stricter case surely does
I did not burn of it while impure (the וידוי מעשר declaration)
Strict, more severe
All the more so

phrases.english: Isn't it a קל וחומר?
If מעשר, which is lenient,
the תורה said
'I did not burn of it while impure,'
then קודש, which is strict, all the more so?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15
steps.terutzMaskana: קודש is stricter than מעשר, so it is surely banned

steps.title: The same logic should include תרומה too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the קל וחומר should also ban burning impure תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, תרומה is also a קל וחומר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the קל וחומר back on itself. תרומה is also holier than מעשר, so it should be banned as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the logic of 'stricter than מעשר' brings in קודש, it should bring in תרומה just the same. Then step 14's leniency for תרומה falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if your logic is right
The portion of produce given to a כהן
Also

phrases.english: If so,
תרומה is also a קל וחומר!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, תְּרוּמָה נָמֵי קַל וָחוֹמֶר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses step 16's logic against step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that impure תרומה may be burned
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תרומה is also holier than מעשר, so the קל וחומר should ban it too

steps.title: The word 'of it' must exclude something
steps.stepSummary: The word 'ממנו' blocks the קל וחומר from reaching everything, so something is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written 'of it'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק says 'ממנו' on purpose. That word limits the rule, so at least one thing must be left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without 'ממנו', the קל וחומר would cover both קודש and תרומה. The word tells us one of them is excluded. Step 19 asks which one, and step 20 answers.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written
Of it, a limiting word

phrases.english: But it is written 'of it'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting word in the פסוק overrides the קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר covers תרומה too
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ממנו' excludes one item from the ban

steps.title: Why exclude תרומה and not קודש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes us decide that 'ממנו' excludes תרומה rather than קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question that sets up the final answer. Why pick תרומה as the excluded item?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both קודש and תרומה are holier than מעשר, and 'ממנו' excludes only one. We need a reason to choose תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see, why did you choose this side

phrases.english: And what did you see?
phrases.notes: What made you decide that 'ממנו' leaves out תרומה and not קודש?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which item 'ממנו' excludes
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason to exclude תרומה rather than קודש

steps.title: קודש has six extra stringencies, so תרומה is excluded
steps.stepSummary: קודש is stricter than תרומה in six ways (פנקעכ"ס), so 'ממנו' must exclude תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that I don't exclude קודש, since it has פנקעכ"ס: פגול, נותר, קרבן, מעילה, כרת, and it is forbidden to an אונן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that it is logical to keep קודש under the ban. קודש has six strict laws that תרומה does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a limiting word must exclude one of two things, we exclude the lighter one. קודש has פגול, נותר, קרבן, מעילה, כרת and is forbidden to an אונן, and none of these apply to תרומה. So impure תרומה oil may be burned, but impure קודש oil may not.

keyTerms.meaning: It is logical, it makes sense
I exclude
A קרבן ruined by a wrong intention about when it will be eaten
Meat of a קרבן left past its time
Misusing holy property for personal benefit
A mourner on the day a close relative dies

steps.whatToRemember: 'ממנו' excludes only one thing from the ban on burning impure holy food. Since קודש has six extra stringencies (פנקעכ"ס), the excluded item is תרומה.

phrases.english: It is logical
that I do not exclude קודש,
since it has פנקעכ"ס:
phrases.notes: This is a memory word. Each letter stands for one of the six strict laws listed next.

phrases.english: פגול, נותר,
קרבן, מעילה,
כרת, and it is forbidden to an אונן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קודש is stricter than תרומה in six ways, so 'ממנו' excludes תרומה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Impure תרומה may be burned as fuel. Impure קודש may not.

steps.title: Maybe תרומה is the stricter one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 20: תרומה has its own four stringencies (מחפ"ז), so maybe 'ממנו' should exclude קודש instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! Maybe I should not exclude תרומה, because it has four stringencies of its own: death, the added fifth, no redemption, and being forbidden to non-כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the argument around. It says תרומה also has strict features that קודש lacks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 showed that קודש has six stringencies over תרומה. Now the גמרא lists four that תרומה has over קודש. If each side has its own stringencies, it is no longer clear which one 'ממנו' should exclude.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the opposite is true
Memory acronym: מִיתָה, חוֹמֶשׁ, פִּדְיוֹן, זָרִים
Death at the hands of Heaven
An added fifth paid by someone who eats תרומה by mistake
Non-כהנים

phrases.english: On the contrary,
it is teruma that I would not exclude
since it has mem-chet-peh-zayin:
phrases.notes: These four letters are a memory aid for the four stringencies listed right after.

phrases.english: death and the added fifth,
and it has no redemption,
and it is forbidden to non-priests!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 20 by listing stringencies that only תרומה has.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 20's claim that קודש is stricter, so 'ממנו' must exclude תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תרומה has four stringencies (מחפ"ז) that קודש lacks, so the comparison does not clearly favor קודש.

steps.title: קודש has more stringencies
steps.stepSummary: קודש's stringencies (six) outnumber תרומה's (four), so קודש counts as stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those, the stringencies of קודש, are more numerous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by counting: six stringencies beat four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side has strict points, but קודש has more of them. So the strict ban stays on קודש, and 'ממנו' still excludes תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: They are more numerous

phrases.english: Those are more numerous.
phrases.notes: "Those" means קודש's six stringencies from the previous step, which outnumber תרומה's four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תרומה's four stringencies might make it equal to or stricter than קודש.
steps.terutzMaskana: קודש has more stringencies, so it is stricter, and 'ממנו' excludes תרומה.

steps.title: כרת outweighs everything
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: קודש carries the punishment of כרת, which is more severe than anything תרומה has.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: כרת is weightier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way to answer, without counting at all. The single fact that קודש carries כרת makes it the stricter one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating קודש while impure brings כרת. Eating תרומה while impure brings only מיתה בידי שמים. כרת is the more severe punishment, so that one difference settles the question.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say instead (introduces another answer)
Being cut off spiritually; a punishment from Heaven
Is weightier, more important

steps.whatToRemember: 'ממנו' excludes תרומה, not קודש, because קודש is stricter: it either has more stringencies or carries כרת.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
karet is weightier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the challenge of Step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each side's stringencies might balance out.
steps.terutzMaskana: כרת is the most severe point, so קודש is stricter.

steps.title: No lashes for impure תרומה, but what is the source for the prohibition?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that impure מעשר brings lashes but impure תרומה does not. It infers that there is still a prohibition for תרומה and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one who eats them while they themselves are impure gets lashes, which is not so with תרומה. So with תרומה he just does not get lashes, but there is still a prohibition. Where do we learn that from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to another line of the earlier משנה. It reads the line carefully and asks for a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says that eating impure תרומה brings no lashes. It does not say eating it is allowed. That wording implies a prohibition still exists, and the גמרא wants to know which פסוק it comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: When the food itself is impure
Receives lashes
From where do we learn this?

phrases.english: and one who eats them while they themselves are impure is flogged,
phrases.notes: "Them" means מעשר שני and ביכורים, from the משנה quoted earlier.

phrases.english: which is not so with teruma.
It is lashes that he does not receive,
but there is a prohibition —
from where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִילְקָא הוּא דְּלָא לָקֵי, הָא אִיסּוּרָא אִיכָּא — מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the same משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that eating impure תרומה is forbidden even though it brings no lashes.

steps.title: The source is a לאו הבא מכלל עשה
steps.stepSummary: The prohibition comes from 'בשעריך תאכלנו': this may be eaten impure, but not other holy food. A prohibition that comes out of a positive command counts as a positive command, so there are no lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Within your gates you shall eat it.' This one may be eaten that way, but not another. A prohibition that comes out of a positive command is treated as a positive command.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source and also explains why there are no lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'it' in the פסוק limits the permission to eat while impure to this case only, so other holy food is forbidden. That prohibition is only implied by a positive command. It is not a full לא תעשה, so it counts as an עשה, and lashes are not given for an עשה.

keyTerms.meaning: For this and not for another
A prohibition implied by a positive command

steps.whatToRemember: Eating impure תרומה is forbidden, but it brings no lashes, because the prohibition is a לאו הבא מכלל עשה, which counts as an עשה.
steps.confusionAlert: 'No lashes' does not mean 'permitted.' The act is still forbidden, just without lashes as a punishment.

phrases.english: The verse states: "Within your gates you shall eat it" —
for this, and not for another.
And a prohibition that comes from a positive command —
is a positive command.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is 'בשעריך תאכלנו': this and not another. Since it is a לאו הבא מכלל עשה, it counts as an עשה and brings no lashes.

steps.title: רב אשי: the first part of the משנה also shows the תנא left things out
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי begins to prove from the first part of the משנה that the תנא did not list every difference. The proof continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: From the first part of the משנה you can also learn that the תנא taught some differences and left others out, since he does not teach...
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי is setting up a proof. He is about to point to a difference the משנה did not list, and the details come right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said the משנה's list was not complete (תנא ושייר). רב אשי adds support for that from a different place in the same משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: From the first part
He taught some and left some out
Since he does not teach

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
from the first part as well you can learn
that he taught and left out —
from the fact that he does not teach

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מֵרֵישָׁא נָמֵי שָׁמְעַתְּ מִינַּהּ דִּתְנָא וְשַׁיַּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the earlier claim that the משנה's list is incomplete and starts adding support for it.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה taught only some differences (תנא ושייר)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The first part of the same משנה, which also leaves out a difference
